ratings.reviewer_notes: Human MDD meta-analysis evaluating IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, CRP, TNF-α, and IFN-γ; IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, and SSRI-specific IL-1β decreased with treatment.
Review concerns inflammatory cytokines in schizophrenia rather than major depressive disorder.
Human systematic review and meta-analysis directly compares CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β in depressed versus healthy adults, including sex-specific associations.
Meta-analysis focuses on PTSD; MDD appears only as a comorbidity considered in subgroup analysis.
Large human cohort links IL-6 and glycoprotein acetyls to anhedonia and atypical energy-related depressive symptoms, but the abstract does not restrict the sample to current MDD.
Review explicitly identifies elevated CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α in clinically relevant MDD subgroups, while also covering bipolar disorder and mechanistic pathways.
Randomized human MDD study stratified participants by CRP and measured IL-6, IL-10, and TNF responses; high CRP was associated with a stronger IL-6 and anhedonia response to LPS.
Aging-focused epidemiologic review notes depression among factors associated with elevated inflammatory markers and discusses IL-6, CRP, and TNF-α, but does not specifically evaluate MDD.
Meta-analysis in elderly people with depression found elevated IL-6 and initially IL-1β, but the record does not clearly specify MDD and also covers Alzheimer's disease.
Direct MDD case-control meta-analysis found significantly higher blood sIL-2R, TNF-α, and IL-6 in patients than controls.
Prospective human study of treatment-resistant major depressive episodes evaluated CRP, IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α; baseline IL-6 predicted ECT outcome, with sex-specific findings for IL-6 and CRP.

Systematic review of perinatal depression reports associations mainly with elevated IL-6, IL-8, CRP, and TNF-α, but included both diagnosed depression and symptom-scale studies rather than MDD exclusively.
Meta-analysis found positive associations of depression with CRP, IL-6, IL-1, and IL-1ra in clinical and community samples, but was not limited to diagnosed MDD.
Study of 1,077 people with current MDD directly evaluates CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, and glycoprotein acetyls in relation to atypical energy-related symptoms and immunometabolic dysregulation.
Narrative review of comorbid obesity and MDD describes elevated CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α as part of shared inflammation, but the obesity-specific context limits direct applicability to MDD generally.

Human case-control MDD study directly reports altered immune-related gene expression and CRP-stratified differences in cytokine proteins including IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12/23p40, IL-16, IL-17A, IFN-γ, and TNF-α.
Direct cumulative meta-analysis confirms higher IL-6 and CRP in MDD; TNF-α was heterogeneous and IL-1β showed no consistent association.
Human MDD meta-analysis directly examines inflammatory markers and antidepressant outcomes, finding lower baseline IL-8 in responders and responder-specific decreases in TNF-α.
Direct meta-analysis of first-episode and antidepressant-naive MDD reports elevations of IL-6, IL-2, TNF-α, IL-4, IL-10, and IFN-γ, with sample-source differences for several cytokines.
Systematic review directly evaluates CRP in depression and MDD, reporting higher CRP with symptom severity, particular symptom patterns, and worse treatment response.
Conference symposium record has no abstract or article-specific evidence concerning inflammatory markers in MDD.
